description: What the SeeBand desktop application passes to its calculations, per model and fit mode. Input for model descriptions in C8. Do not edit by hand without checking the cited source.

scale_rules.calc: value passed to the curve calculation on the slider handler path = slider * calc_scale; see calc_paths for other paths
scale_rules.internal_factor: internal_fit_factor multiplies both the start value and the bounds for acPhDis; results are divided on return where returned_divided_source is set

bounds_note: default_fit_bounds are the values at startup. With bounds_origin slider_range, fits read the live slider range, and Advanced options can change it where editable is true. Qt then clamps the current slider value, so changing a range can also change a start value, including the fixed SPB mass.

data_preparation.fits_read: interpolated_*_data, which starts as the raw data
data_preparation.switch_off: Rebuilds the mask from the raw data but keeps the interpolated values (D16)

adjust_to_fit.effect: Writes fit results back to the sliders, which become the next start values

deviations.title: DPB S + rho + R_H with dis passes G bounds in slider units
deviations.desktop: Start is 1.0 (slider / 100), bounds stay 50 to 200, so the fit stops with `Initial guess is outside of provided bounds`. Confirmed on the real window for all 3 examples. In S + rho the bounds are scaled. With a G slider minimum of 1 the fit returns a result, but it is not credible on 2 of the 3 examples. By reading the code, a lower limit of 0.01 in Advanced options gives that minimum.
deviations.web: Use bounds 0.5 to 2. This is a deliberate deviation in the GUI layer.

deviations.title: SPB S + rho + R_H always fails
deviations.desktop: The fit reads `fermi_slider_spb`, which does not exist, so the thread stops with an error.
deviations.web: Mode disabled until fixed.

deviations.title: SPB S + rho + R_H handles the mass parameter incorrectly
deviations.desktop: The slider value is passed without dividing by 100, with raw slider bounds. For m > 0 the start expression gives an empty list. The start uses -sign and the bounds +sign, and the result curve flips the sign of m.
deviations.web: Fixed with the mode.

deviations.title: SPB C has three different scales
deviations.desktop: Displayed as slider / 100, but the fit and the S + rho slider curve use the raw slider value, then multiply by 300 for acPhDis.
deviations.web: Exact port keeps the numbers. Describe C in core units and flag acPhDis results.

deviations.title: SPB S + rho + R_H slider curve multiplies C by 300 twice
deviations.desktop: The slider handler passes slider * 300, and the calculation multiplies by 300 again for acPhDis. The line-edit handler passes the raw value.
deviations.web: Fixed with the mode.

deviations.title: SPB S + rho + R_H returns C without dividing by 300
deviations.desktop: S + rho divides by 300 on return and S + rho + R_H does not, while the calculation multiplies by 300 again. The code calls this value `current_para_B`.
deviations.web: Fixed with the mode.

deviations.title: SPB S + rho + R_H result curve passes too few parameters
deviations.desktop: The curve after a fit passes `params[1:3]`, while S + rho passes `params[1:4]`. Only acPh returns a curve: dis fails because no parameter is left, and acPhDis fails because C is removed and then indexed.
deviations.web: Fixed with the mode.

deviations.title: Iteration settings differ between DPB modes
deviations.desktop: S + rho hardcodes 0.1 and 1000. S + rho + R_H uses 0.1 and 20 from the main window. Neither can be changed in a window.
deviations.web: Exact port keeps these per-mode values in the model description.

deviations.title: Advanced options for SPB parameter A write to DPB variables
deviations.desktop: The SPB S + rho handler sets `para_A_*_limit_dpb_res`. The S + rho + R_H handler changes `para_A_slider_dpb_hall`, and so the DPB Hall lower bound for A. Limits entered for SPB A never reach an SPB fit.
deviations.web: Not ported. Editable bounds apply to the selected mode.

deviations.title: Main-window limit variables are not used by DPB fits
deviations.desktop: `para_*_limit_dpb_*` on the main window are initialised but DPB fits read slider ranges. Advanced options windows have their own same-named fields that feed the sliders. SPB `para_E_*_limit_spb_hall` is not read at all.
deviations.web: Not ported. `default_fit_bounds` records what the fits use by default, and `editable` shows what Advanced options can change.

deviations.title: Defaults and steps differ between windows of the same model
deviations.desktop: SPB mass and E_F start at 1.01 and 100 in S, -1.00 and -100 in S + rho, 1.00 and 100 in S + rho + R_H. The G step is 1 in S + rho and 100 in S + rho + R_H, and the F step is 100 and 1000.
deviations.web: Exact port keeps the defaults. Agree whether to unify them when building the form in FS5.

deviations.title: DPB fits and curves treat m_eff differently when N2/N1 is not 1
deviations.desktop: In S, the fit uses m_eff without dividing by N and returns that value, while the curve divides by N. In S + rho and S + rho + R_H, the fit starts from the slider mass and returns `current_meff*degen`, and the curve divides by N, so the post-fit curve is consistent, but the start is N times the displayed mass and the reported value can leave the bounds. The S + rho + R_H curve also reads N from the S + rho window, while its fit reads its own window.
deviations.web: Exact port keeps this until fixed.

deviations.title: C and D reach the calculation at different scales on different paths
deviations.desktop: See `calc_paths` per mode. For one DPB slider position with acPhDis, an exported curve uses C = 100 * 300 and the slider curve C = 1 * 300.
deviations.web: The web version has one calculation path, in core values, the same as the start and result of a fit. That equals the slider handler scale, apart from `band_mass` and `C` in SPB S + rho + R_H (D3, D5). V1 records differences against desktop exports and startup curves.

deviations.title: A new fit range updates only some data masks
deviations.desktop: `minT` and `maxT` are shared by all windows, and `x_mask` by all fits. Only the DPB S + rho and S + rho + R_H handlers update `x_mask_res`, and only DPB S + rho + R_H updates `x_mask_hall`. In SPB S + rho, a new range restricts the Seebeck fit but not the rho fit, and a range set in one window changes the Seebeck data of the others.
deviations.web: One fit range applies to every quantity of the selected mode. Golden results use the default range, and V1 records the difference.

deviations.title: DPB start values depend on the neural net and on earlier fits
deviations.desktop: Each Seebeck import starts the net, which overwrites mass, gap and E_F in all three DPB windows, if a model matches the temperature span. Adjust to fit writes rounded results back to the sliders. See `start_value_overrides`.
deviations.web: Run the guess after loading S, as on the desktop. C3 uses these start values, not `slider.default`. If no net matches, C3 uses the defaults of a fresh session.

deviations.title: Switching interpolation off does not restore the data
deviations.desktop: The mask is rebuilt from the raw data, but `interpolated_*_data` keeps the interpolated values, so a later fit indexes one array with a mask built from another.
deviations.web: Not ported. Turning it off restores the original data.

deviations.title: SPB scattering handlers read the DPB combo boxes
deviations.desktop: Switching SPB back to acPh takes the wrong branch unless the DPB box also says acPh, so controls and redraws can be stale. Fits use the correct box, so fit numbers are unaffected.
deviations.web: Not ported. Controls follow the selected mode.

deviations.title: DPB acPhDis can stop when only part of the parameters converged
deviations.desktop: The loop stops when m_eff, gap, E_F, A and B converge, or when C and D alone converge. Both groups are needed. On the real window, every acPhDis fit on the 3 examples stopped on C and D alone, after 1 or 2 iterations. Relative change also divides by the previous value, which fails at 0.
deviations.web: Exact port keeps this until fixed.

deviations.title: DPB fits on 02_SiP differ between library versions and machines
deviations.desktop: m_eff collapses towards 0 on every version. In the golden results the rho stage then stays at its start, with A = 40000, so the rho curve is about 1e-11 against data of 0.016 to 0.16, although A of about 1e-5 would match the data. On the project's versions A reached about 1e-5 for acPh and acPhDis on one Mac. On Linux CI it did so for acPh but stayed far off for acPhDis, so the result depends on the machine.
deviations.web: These fits cannot match the desktop reliably, and differ by up to about 9 orders of magnitude in A. Treat them as unsound. V1 records this, and a physicist should see the results.

deviations.title: Additional graphs pass C and D at other scales than the fit
deviations.desktop: The buttons of the additional graphs windows read the sliders. With acPhDis they pass SPB C = slider / 100 and DPB C and D = slider, while the fit start passes SPB C = slider and DPB C and D = slider / 100. So at one slider position, these graphs use C and D 100 times apart from the fit, on top of the mismatch in P3.
deviations.web: Curves take core values, so graphs use the same C and D as the fit and the main curve, and results of a fit go to graphs unchanged. Recorded graph calls replay with their recorded values. V1 records the differences.

deviations.title: Reaching the iteration limit looks like success
deviations.desktop: When an iterative DPB fit reaches its limit, it stops after the Seebeck fit of the extra iteration, and returns results without an error. Only `print_info` showed this.
deviations.web: The fit returns the same values with the status `iteration_limit`.

deviations.title: The web parser rejects bad lines and sorts by temperature
deviations.desktop: The parser drops any line it cannot read, without saying so, and fails on two spaces in a row or a comma followed by a space. It keeps the order of the rows, so the neural net choice reads the first and last rows as the range.
deviations.web: A line it cannot read is an error with its line number, and these separators work. Rows are sorted by temperature with a warning. So an unsorted file can get a net where the desktop gets none, as P9 intends, and solver starts follow the new order.
